info.title: hashinbox-api
info.description: The hashinbox HTTP routes and OpenAPI contract over the chain-neutral wallet and index abstractions. An asset is its network's own asset id (`native`, or a token); no chain or asset is named in this contract.

get.summary: Read readiness and every indexed network's indexing
get.description: Public readiness: ready when at least one network has an index, every indexed network has an enabled RPC node, and no network's index job has a reason (`job_reason`: it failed, or goes again because of it). Reads the stored networks; no RPC.
The contract every route is generated from; public, like the health routes.

500.description: The contract could not be encoded

get.description: Every asset of every configured network, with its metadata. This is the only list of assets the wallet routes accept.

parameters.name: chain
parameters.description: Only jobs of this chain; with `network`.

parameters.name: network
parameters.description: Only jobs of this network of `chain`.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only jobs in this state; absent, every state but `idle`.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

400.description: Malformed query, cursor, or limit, or a chain without its network

get.description: The job's outcome, what it was given and what its worker has done; for a broadcast, the transaction it recorded and whether it was sent.

The kept entries the filters read, newest first, a page at a time: its level, event (`target`), own message (null: its template's, `/v1/logs/messages`) and fields, and its network, job, wallet, transaction, trigger and market when it has them. With `after`, oldest first from that moment, so a reader can page forward from a time. Debug and trace entries are kept 24 hours, the rest 30 days; at most the newest 10 000 of a job, and of a network's (or no network's) entries outside a job.

parameters.name: wallet_id
parameters.description: Only entries of this wallet, its id (`{chain}.{network}.{address}`).

parameters.name: transaction_id
parameters.description: Only entries of this transaction, its id (`{chain}.{network}.{txid}`).

parameters.name: trigger_id
parameters.description: Only entries of this trigger, its id.

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Only entries of this market, its name (`binance`).

parameters.name: level
parameters.description:
Only entries at this level or more severe: `error`, `warn`, `info`,
`debug` or `trace`.

parameters.name: only
parameters.description: With `level`: only entries at exactly that level.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Only entries of these events, comma-separated (`rpc.http,index.leg`).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only entries from before this Unix ms.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only entries from this Unix ms on; a page then lists oldest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

400.description: Malformed query, level, network, cursor, or limit

get.description: Every event's (`target`) message template, by which a log entry with no `message` of its own reads: each `{key}` filled from its field `key`. An event without a template reads as its code and its fields. They change only with the server, so the answer may be cached.

`text/event-stream` of every entry kept from now on that the filters read (those of the list): one event per entry, its `data` a `LogEntry` (its `id` 0: not yet stored). A reader too slow for the feed gets `event: missed` with `{"missed": n}`, then the entries after. Comments keep the connection alive; the stream does not end.

parameters.name: wallet_id
parameters.description: Only entries of this wallet, its id (`{chain}.{network}.{address}`).

parameters.name: transaction_id
parameters.description: Only entries of this transaction, its id (`{chain}.{network}.{txid}`).

parameters.name: trigger_id
parameters.description: Only entries of this trigger, its id.

parameters.name: market
parameters.description: Only entries of this market, its name (`binance`).

parameters.name: level
parameters.description:
Only entries at this level or more severe: `error`, `warn`, `info`,
`debug` or `trace`.

parameters.name: only
parameters.description: With `level`: only entries at exactly that level.

parameters.name: target
parameters.description: Only entries of these events, comma-separated (`rpc.http,index.leg`).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only entries from before this Unix ms.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Only entries from this Unix ms on; a page then lists oldest first.

200.description: The entries, as they are kept

get.description: Every event (`target`) a kept entry has, each once, in order: the values the `target` filter of the log lists and the stream takes.

get.summary: List the markets and the latest prices
get.description: Every market data source: its name, whether it is asked for quotes (`feed`), when it was last changed and when its last quote answered (`last_at`); and, by ticker, each asset's latest USD price: the median close of the current hour's candles.

patch.summary: Turn a market's feed on or off
patch.description: Stores whether the market is asked for quotes; the market job reads it on its next tick (within 10 s).

get.summary: List a market's hourly candles of an asset
get.description: The market's own hourly USD candles of the asset (open, high, low and close of its quotes) from `after` on, at most the last 7 days, oldest first; the current hour's moves until the hour ends.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description:
Only the hours starting at or after this, Unix seconds; at most the
last 7 days.

get.summary: List every network, its assets, its RPC nodes, its indexing and its tip
get.description: Every stored network: its row, its assets, its routes, its nodes (each URL with its calls and, while disabled, the record that disabled it: `disabled`) and its `index` (its `network_index` row and why its index job last failed, `job_reason`; null: neither). `tip.live` is the highest tip its nodes last told, kept in memory: no node is asked.

503.description: The networks could not be read

post.description: Stores a network and its native currency in one write, checked by its chain as a start reads it, then registers it at once, with no node: add its nodes with `POST /v1/networks/{chain}/{network}/endpoints`, and it indexes from then on.

400.description: Malformed body, a name that is not a slug, an unknown chain, or a network its chain refuses

503.description: The network could not be stored

post.summary: Add RPC nodes to one or more networks
post.description: Appends each node after its network's current ones, stores every changed list in one write (all or none), then sends every later call of those networks to their new lists. A provider's nodes for several networks are added at once this way.

400.description: Malformed node, a list above 16 nodes, or a node that fails or serves another chain

503.description: The nodes could not be stored

get.summary: List a network's last kept blocks
get.description: Live kept blocks, latest first, a page at a time.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

get.summary: Read one kept block of a network

404.description: The network is not configured, or no live block is kept at this position

get.summary: List a live block's kept transactions

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

404.description: The network is not configured, or no live block is kept at this position

get.description: Its stored nodes in stored order: each one's id, URL (as `PUT` takes it) and position, its calls (`stats`, each written as it finishes) and, while disabled, the record that disabled it (`disabled`: its kind and why; null: enabled).

503.description: The nodes could not be read

put.description: Stores the nodes, then sends every later call of the network (indexing, wallets, broadcast) to them: the healthy node with the highest tip first, then the others in order; calls already sent finish on the node they reached. Each node is asked its chain and tip once, before storing. A URL already stored keeps its id, routes and state; one left out is removed with its routes.

400.description: Malformed node list, or a node that fails or serves another chain

503.description: The nodes could not be stored

post.summary: Add RPC nodes to a network
post.description: Appends the nodes after the network's current ones, stores the list, then sends every later call of the network to it.

400.description: Malformed node, a list above 16 nodes, or a node that fails or serves another chain

503.description: The nodes could not be stored

post.summary: Test an RPC node against a network, without adding it
post.description: Asks the node its chain and tip once, as adding it would, and answers them; nothing is stored. A node that fails, or serves another chain, is refused with why (its chain id said).

400.description: Malformed URL, or a node that fails or serves another chain

delete.summary: Remove one RPC node of a network
delete.description: Removes the node `id` and its routes, stores the rest and uses them from now on. A network's last node cannot be removed.

404.description: No such node, or network not configured

422.description: It is the network's last node

503.description: The nodes could not be stored

get.summary: List what disabled or enabled one RPC node
get.description: Every failure of the node it cannot recover from (which disabled it: `http_401`, `http_403`, `http_404`, `wrong_chain`, ...) and every disable or enable by hand (`manual`, `enabled`), newest first, a page at a time: when, the kind and why. The newest is its state. A failure it may recover from (a rate limit, a timeout) is in the logs (`rpc.http`).

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

404.description: No such node, or network not configured

put.summary: Enable or disable one RPC node of a network
put.description: Stores why (a `manual` record disables, an `enabled` one enables), then sends every later call of the network to its enabled nodes only; a route skips a disabled node. Disabling the last enabled node is allowed: the network's index job idles and its payments wait until one is enabled again. Asks no node.

404.description: No such node, or network not configured

503.description: The state could not be stored

get.description: Each routed method and the nodes taking turns serving it, round robin. Every other method goes to the network's healthy node with the highest tip.

503.description: The routes could not be read

put.description: Stores the routes, then sends each routed method round robin over its nodes, and every other method to the healthy node with the highest tip. A routed call failing retryably moves to the next node, then to the network's other nodes. No node is asked.

400.description: An empty method, a method routed twice, or a node that is missing, repeated or of another network

503.description: The routes could not be stored

get.summary: Find a network's last block at or before a time, streaming the search
get.description: `text/event-stream`, read from the node: `event: probe` with `{"low":{"position","timestamp"},"high":{…}}` after each step of the binary search (the range narrows: the block is at or after `low`, before `high`); then `event: found` with `{"position","timestamp"}`, or `event: error` with `{"message"}` (cannot find blocks by time, before the first block, the node failed). The stream then ends.

parameters.name: at
parameters.description:
RFC 3339 time (`2026-10-01T00:00:00Z`) or Unix seconds: find the last
block at or before it.

get.summary: List a network's transactions, or only its pending ones

parameters.name: pending
parameters.description:
Only pending ones (true), oldest sent first; otherwise (the default)
pending and mined in live blocks, newest first.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

get.summary: Read whether the recovery passphrase is set
get.description: Whether a passphrase is set and when it was created; never its words or hash. Needs `recovery.$write`, as the other recovery routes do.

post.summary: Create or replace the recovery passphrase
post.description: 12 new BIP39 words, answered this once, in place of any passphrase set; only their argon2id hash is kept. Replacing ends every session the old words made (`session_expired`). They sign in as any user (`POST /v1/session` with `passphrase`), two-factor still asked: whoever holds them is every user without two-factor.

delete.description: Passphrase logins are off (refused as wrong credentials) and every session the words made ends (`session_expired`). 204 when none is set too.

get.description: The session the bearer token is, decoded and checked: its issuer, user, key, scopes, times and `amr`.

post.summary: Log in, or sign a key's session
post.description: With `email` and `password` or `passphrase` (the recovery passphrase, any user's email; and `totp` once two-factor is on) and no `Authorization`: a session of the user, its scopes or fewer, its `amr` `pwd` or `passphrase` (and `otp`). A wrong email, password, passphrase or code answers the same 401; the rest right without the code answers 401 `totp_required`. With `Authorization: Bearer his/…`: a session of the key, signed here, for a caller that cannot sign (`sub`, `scopes` covered by the key's).

400.description: Malformed body, scopes or ttl; neither or both of password and passphrase

401.description: Wrong email, password, passphrase or code (`wrong_credentials`), or `totp_required`

delete.description: Alone, nothing: the client forgets its token. With `all=true`, every session the caller's issuer (its user, or its key) issued until now answers 401, this one too.

parameters.name: all
parameters.description:
Every session the issuer (the user, or the key) issued until now:
refused.

get.description: Every setting the server declares: its key, value (its default when never written), default, whether it is public, description and type. A secret setting (`recovery_passphrase`) shows only its key, whether it is set and its description.

put.description: Stores the setting's value once it parses as the setting's type and passes its check. Whether it is public is the declaration's, never the request's. A secret setting is never written here: 403 `permission_denied`.

400.description: Malformed body, unknown key, wrong type or refused value

403.description: Missing scope, or a secret setting

get.summary: Read what the store holds and its last day
get.description: Counts across every network, and per hour over the last day: blocks and transactions by chain time (up to the newest kept block), jobs and trigger runs by this server's time.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

post.description: Stores every trigger or none, all on one configured network, each with an `id` chosen here that never changes: a template of several triggers (gas funding and sweep) never lands half.

400.description: Malformed body or id, a repeated id, several networks, or a send from This to This

404.description: Network or sent asset is not configured

put.description: Replaces everything but its id and creation time; a body `id` is refused. Setting `enabled` to false pauses it.

400.description: Malformed body, or a send from This to This

404.description: No such trigger, or network not configured

delete.summary: Delete a trigger and its runs

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

get.description: The caller's user, its scopes and its two-factor; the calling key too, when a key calls.

put.description: Sets a new password, checked as at signup; the current one is not asked, so any session of the user (a passphrase login too) may. Every other session it and its keys issued ends (401); the answer is a fresh session, the caller's scopes and `amr`.

400.description: Malformed body, or a password too short

post.description: A new TOTP secret, pending until its first code is confirmed (`POST /v1/user/2fa/confirm`); starting again replaces a pending one.

delete.description: Needs a valid code; logs the user out everywhere.

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer token, or a wrong code

post.description: Its first valid code turns two-factor on: a login needs a code from now.

401.description: Missing or invalid bearer token, or a wrong code

get.description: The caller's user's keys, revoked ones too, a page in id order; never a secret.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

post.description: A key of the caller's user, its scopes covered by the caller's. Its secret is in this answer only.

403.description: Missing scope, or scopes wider than the caller's

delete.description: The key (its secret) and every session it signed answer 401 for good. `id` is the key's id without `hip/`.

404.description: No such key of the caller's user, or revoked already

post.description: Every session the key signed until now answers 401; the key itself keeps working. `id` is the key's id without `hip/`.

404.description: No such key of the caller's user

get.description: Every user, a page in id order; never a password or a secret.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

post.summary: Create a user, or the root user on a fresh install
post.description: With no user yet (`GET /v1/version` says `missing_root`), needs no `Authorization`: creates the root user, holding every scope, logged in at once (its session in the answer); of two racing, one is root and the other answers 409. Else needs `users.$write`, and the new user's scopes must be covered by the caller's.

400.description: Malformed body, email, name, password or scopes

403.description: Missing scope, or scopes wider than the caller's

409.description: The email is taken, or the root user exists

patch.summary: Change a user's scopes, or disable it
patch.description: Narrowing a user narrows its keys and sessions at once: one wider than its user answers 401 from the next request on.

403.description: Missing scope, or scopes wider than the caller's

get.description: Public: the version this server was built as, `missing_root` while no user exists (`POST /v1/users` creates the root) and every public setting's value. A 200 means the server is up and serving.

Keyed wallets and watched addresses, a page in wallet ID order, each with its tags and its indexes: their balances (exact atomic units), progress and legs. A caller granted only some wallets reads each by its ID.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

post.summary: Import a wallet's key, watch an address, or generate a wallet, in one configured network
post.description: With `secret`, imports a raw private key and keeps it; with `address` too, the key must derive that address. With `address` alone, watches it without its key. With neither, generates a key and keeps it; retrying makes another wallet. The wallet is created without indexes (`POST /v1/wallets/{id}/index`). An address already kept answers its wallet as is (200), except that importing the key of a watch-only wallet keeps the key, and an `external_id` is kept on a wallet that has none; another `external_id` than the kept one is refused (409); its tags and indexes stay.

200.description: The address was already kept: its wallet

400.description: Malformed body, address, key or external ID, or a key that derives another address

409.description: The address is kept with another external ID

503.description: Generation or the store is unavailable

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

get.description: The wallet's network, canonical address, whether it is keyed, the assets it is indexed in and how far each is; never its key.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `{chain}.{network}.{address}`, as a create call returned it.

post.summary: Index a wallet in an asset
post.description: Indexes the wallet in `asset` from `start` (absent: the chain's tip), at once (the network's next indexing step picks it). An asset already indexed keeps its first start (200). A `start` above the chain's tip, or below it less the network's `max_depth`, is refused (400). On a chain that reads balances (Solana, Ethereum) the index starts at the chain's final block whatever `start` says (kept as `requested_from`): its balances are null until the chain's balance read there opens it with an `adjustment` leg. A start the node no longer serves moves forward to the first block it serves before indexing begins.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: `{chain}.{network}.{address}`, as a create call returned it.

200.description: The asset was already indexed: its index

400.description: Malformed body or wallet ID, or a start above the chain's tip or below it less the network's `max_depth`

404.description: Wallet is unknown, or the asset is not configured

503.description: The node or the store is unavailable

delete.summary: Stop indexing a wallet in an asset
delete.description: Forgets the index and its progress: its balance and history are no longer read. Creating it again starts from its new start.

patch.summary: Pause or resume a wallet's index
patch.description: `paused`: skipped, no facts kept for blocks while paused; what is kept stays. `indexing`: from `paused` or `no_data` (clearing its reason), it continues from its last indexed block, backfilling what it missed. On a chain that reads balances (Solana, Ethereum) one left behind the chain's final block is not read back: its balance is read there and one `adjustment` leg closes the gap.

400.description: Malformed body or wallet ID, or `no_data` asked for

get.description: The index's legs in live blocks, latest first, each with the balance right after it. Its pending legs are on the index itself.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page; absent for the first page.

400.description: Malformed wallet ID, query, cursor, or limit

post.summary: Reconcile a wallet's index with the chain's balance
post.description: Deletes the index's mined legs above the chain's final block and unsets its progress: its balances read null until the next indexing step reads the chain's balance at a final block, appends one `adjustment` leg of the difference and reads on from there. Pending legs stay. Corrects what indexing cannot see, such as ether a contract sent. Only on chains that read balances (Solana, Ethereum).

422.description: The chain reads no balance (Bitcoin), or the index is paused or `no_data`

503.description: The indexer has not read the chain's final block yet, or the store is unavailable

put.description: Tags the wallet, keyed or watch-only; tagging twice keeps one tag.

404.description: Wallet is unknown, or network not configured

delete.description: Removes the tag from the wallet.

404.description: No such wallet or tag, or network not configured

post.summary: Enqueue a payment from a wallet
post.description: Enqueues one send job of `asset` from the keyed wallet: one payment, signed as one transaction and broadcast. Several payments are several requests; a wallet's sends run one at a time, in order, and each fails on its own. A 202 response means queued, not submitted: `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` reports the outcome. Indexing records the transaction once it is mined, for the assets the wallet is watched in. A watch-only wallet answers 422, as does a wallet whose index of `asset` (and, for a token, of `native`, which pays the fee) is missing: there is no balance to check. A paused index still sends, and its transaction is recorded once mined.

400.description: Malformed body, wallet ID, amount, or destination

404.description: Network or asset is not configured

422.description: A watch-only or unknown wallet, or a sender index missing

503.description: The queue or store is unavailable

Amr.description:
How a user session's login proved who it is: the JWT's standard `amr`
claim (RFC 8176), each method once.

Asset.description: Metadata of the asset an amount is denominated in.

decimals.description: Decimal places between atomic and display units.

display_decimals.description: Fractional digits a view shows; always present, null: all.

id.description: Asset ID within the chain (`native` or a token identifier).

name.description: Display name, when known; always present.

ticker.description: Ticker symbol, when known; always present.

assets.description: Assets in network, then id, order.

Block.description:
A kept block: its `block` row; the API shows it as is. Written with its
kept transactions in block order and its kept rewards, which are never
read back into it.

parent.description: Its parent's id, once that is kept.

parent_position.description: Its parent's position; null for genesis.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

BlockTransactions.description:
`GET /v1/networks/{chain}/{network}/blocks/{position}/transactions`: a
page of a block's transactions.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

transactions.description: The transactions, with their legs, in block order.

ChainHour.description: One hour of chain time, across every network.

transactions.description: Kept transactions mined in those blocks.

ConfiguredNetwork.description: One stored network, and its tip as its nodes last told it.

expires_at.description: Unix ms it stops working; never when absent.

name.description: What it is for, 1 to 128 characters: `shop backend`.

scopes.description:
Its scopes, packed, covered by the caller's; the caller's when
absent.

CreateSession.description:
`POST /v1/session` body: `email` and `password` or `passphrase` (and
`totp`) log in; with `Authorization: Bearer his/…`, the key's session,
for `sub`.

passphrase.description:
A login: the recovery passphrase (12 words, any spacing or case),
for any user; or `password`, not both.

password.description: A login: the user's password; or `passphrase`, not both.

scopes.description:
Fewer scopes than the issuer's, packed
(`{"com.hashinbox": ["wallets[x].$read"]}`); the issuer's when
absent.

sub.description:
A key's session: who it is for (a customer); logged, grants
nothing.

totp.description: A login: the 6-digit two-factor code, when it is on.

ttl.description: Seconds it lasts, 1 to 86400; 43200 when absent.

password.description:
Its password, 8 characters at least; absent: no dashboard login
(the root user needs one).

scopes.description:
Its scopes, packed, covered by the creator's; none when absent.
The root user holds every scope.

CreateWallet.description:
`POST /v1/wallets` body: a wallet in one network, created without
indexes. With `secret`, its key is imported and kept; else with
`address`, the address is watched without a key; with neither, a new key
is generated and kept.

address.description:
Address text in any form the chain accepts; with `secret`, the
address the key must derive.

external_id.description:
Your own reference for the wallet (e.g. your customer id), 1 to 128
characters once trimmed; not unique.

secret.description:
A raw private key in the chain's import format: Ethereum hex, Solana
Base58 secret or keypair, Bitcoin WIF.

asset.description: The asset id to index the wallet in.

start.description:
The native position to index from, at or below the chain's tip and
at or above the tip less the network's `max_depth` (a chain that
reads balances starts at its final block instead). Absent: from the chain's tip, as a generated
wallet (it has no past) must be.

CreatedKey.description: A key created, and its secret, shown this once.

secret.description:
`his/…`: its secret, never shown again. A bearer token as it is, and
the HS256 key, as it is, of the sessions the key signs (`kid` and
`iss`: the key's id).

CreatedUser.description: A user created; the root user logged in at once.

token.description:
The root user's session (a fresh install only): send it as
`Authorization: Bearer …`.

Error.description:
A failure: its kind, its message, and what a client acts on. The body of
every error response.

kind.description: What kind of failure: the response's status follows from it.

metadata.description: Details of the reason, as strings: `{"scope": "…"}`.

reason.description:
A fixed machine string a client acts on: `wrong_credentials`,
`totp_required`, `session_expired`, `missing_scope`.

FeeLevel.description:
How fast a payment should land: `low`, `normal` and `high` pay the
network's rate now with its tip × 0.5, 1 or 2 (Ethereum's priority fee,
Bitcoin's rate above the mempool minimum, Solana's priority price); the
base part (Ethereum's base fee, Bitcoin's mempool minimum) is the
network's, so `low` is never below what nodes accept.

token.description: The JWT: send it as `Authorization: Bearer …`.

accepted.description: Whether it was sent: a node accepted it, or may hold it (false for other kinds).

attempts.description: Executions started since it was last fresh.

created_at.description: When it was queued, Unix ms.

deadline.description: Not started after this, Unix ms; always present.

input.description: What it was given; null for a kind given nothing (`prune`).

progress.description: What its worker has done so far; always present.

reason.description:
Why it failed, or why its last attempt is being retried; always
present.

run_at.description: Not started before this, Unix ms: the next run of a pending job.

topic.description: What it locks: jobs whose topics conflict run one at a time, in line order.

txid.description:
A broadcast's transaction (txid), once recorded; always present,
null before and for other kinds.

updated_at.description: When it was last written, Unix ms: started, retried or finished.

jobs.description: The jobs last written, latest first.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

keys.description: The caller's user's keys, in id order.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

Kind.description:
What kind of failure an [`Error`] is: gRPC's status codes, each one
HTTP status.

confirmed.description: The confirmed block position it decided at.

refused.description: Why it was refused (it then acted on nothing); always present.

LastRound.description: A trigger's last round, whether it acted or not.

Leg.description:
One `leg` row: a transaction's leg, a block's reward, or an index's
adjustment; the API shows it as is.

amount.description: Exact atomic decimal text; signed for a reward or an adjustment.

amount_usd.description:
Its value in USD, exact decimal, signed as it adds to the balance
(negative for a spent, burned or fee leg): `amount` in display units
times its asset's USD price at its hour (its block's
time, else when its transaction was recorded) when it was mined;
null when there was none, while pending, and for an adjustment.
Never filled later.

archived_at.description:
A received coin a jump wrote off: that jump's position; never
spendable again. Null otherwise.

block.description: Its block; null while pending, and for an adjustment.

kind.description:
0 received, 1 spent, 2 burned, 3 minted, 4 fee, 5 reward, 6
adjustment (signed; leg 0: what the chain's balance read corrects the
index's total by, at the position it was read at; leg 1: the coins a
jump archived).

position.description: Its block's position, or an adjustment's own; `None` while pending.

seq.description:
Its index's leg sequence: 1 + the highest the index has kept,
unique per index; `None` while pending.

total.description: Its index's balance right after it; `None` while pending.

total_received.description:
What its index has received (received, minted, reward) through it;
`None` while pending. No adjustment counts.

total_received_usd.description:
`total_received` in USD: each received leg's `amount_usd` (null: 0)
added; `None` while pending.

total_sent.description:
What its index has sent (spent, burned, fee) through it; `None` while
pending. `total` is `total_received - total_sent` plus its index's
adjustments so far.

total_sent_usd.description:
`total_sent` in USD: each sent leg's `amount_usd` (null: 0) added;
`None` while pending.

transaction.description: Its transaction; null for a reward or an adjustment.

wallet_index_id.description: The wallet index it is kept for: its address's index in its asset.

legs.description:
Live mined legs, latest first, each with the balance after it
(`total`) and its transaction's txid and state (null for a reward).

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

oneOf.description: A public or private setting, its value shown.
A secret setting: never its value.

Listed.description:
A setting as listed: its value, or for a secret one only whether it is
set.

Listing.description: One configured asset: its id, where its wallets live, and what they hold.

asset.description:
The id every wallet route's `asset` takes within `network`: `native`,
or a token's chain-owned id.

network.description: The chain and network this asset's wallets live on.

LiveTip.description: The network's tip as its nodes last told it.

live.description:
The highest tip its nodes last told, kept in memory (asked at most
once per block time, by selection and indexing); the stored
`index.tip` before any node told one. Always present, null: neither.

chain.description: Its network's chain; always present, null: no network's.

fields.description: Its fields and its spans' (`network`, `node`, …), as text.

id.description:
Its id, newest highest; 0 until stored, so 0 on the live stream
(`/v1/logs/stream`).

job_id.description: The job it ran in; always present, null: none.

market.description: The market it concerns (`binance`, …); always present, null: none.

message.description:
The event's own message, in place of its template; always present,
null: none, the template's.

network.description: Its network's name; always present, null: no network's.

target.description:
The event's code: `rpc.http.failed`, `index.step`, … Its message is
its template (`GET /v1/logs/messages`) filled from `fields`.

transaction_id.description:
The transaction it concerns (`{chain}.{network}.{txid}`); always
present, null: none.

trigger_id.description: The trigger it concerns; always present, null: none.

wallet_id.description:
The wallet it concerns (`{chain}.{network}.{address}`); always
present, null: none.

logs.description: The entries, newest first; oldest first with `after`.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

messages.description:
Each event (`target`) and its template: lower case text with
`{key}` placeholders, each filled from the entry's field `key`; a
placeholder of a field the entry lacks stays as it is. An entry's
own `message` takes the place of its template.

LogTargets.description: The events log entries are kept of.

targets.description:
Each event (`target`) once, in order: what a log list's `target`
filter takes.

feed.description: Whether it is asked for quotes.

updated_at.description: Unix ms it was last changed.

MarketCandle1h.description:
One `market_candle_1h` row: open, high, low and close are exact decimal
USD.

updated_at.description: When its last quote answered, Unix ms.

candles.description: The market's hourly candles of the asset, oldest first.

prices.description:
Each asset's latest USD price, exact decimal, by ticker: the median
close of the markets' candles of the current hour; empty until the
market job's first tick after a start.

last_at.description:
When its last quote answered, Unix ms; always present, null: no
candle kept.

MarketListing.description: A market and when it last answered.

timestamp.description: Its block's time, Unix seconds, when the node reported one.

Movement.description:
A mined leg with its transaction's txid and state (null for a reward or
an adjustment) and its block's time: a row of [`db::find_page`].

decimals.description: Fractional digits between the display unit and the atomic unit.

Network.description:
The chain and network a wallet, address, or transaction belongs to. It
always ships as one nested object, never as two sibling fields.

NetworkAsset.description: One asset of a network: its native currency or a token.

contract.description:
The token's contract (mint); always present, null for the native
currency.

decimals.description: Fractional digits between the display unit and the atomic unit.

display_decimals.description: Fractional digits a view shows; always present, null: all.

endpoints.description: Its nodes as stored, in failover order.

networks.description: Networks in chain, then name, order.

enabled_endpoints.description:
How many of its RPC nodes are enabled; 0: no call can go out, its
index job idles (its reason says so) and its payments wait.

oneOf.description:
Its indexing; always present, null: no tip known and no index job
reason yet.

NetworkIndexing.description:
One network's indexing: what its indexer last wrote (its `network_index`
row) and why its index job last failed.

checked_at.description: Unix ms of the indexer's last read whose tip moved; always present.

confirmed.description:
`tip - confirmations` (saturating), written with it; always present,
null with it.

indexed.description: The last kept block; always present, null: none yet.

job_reason.description:
Why its index job's last run failed or idles (the job's `reason`),
cleared by the next run that does not; always present, null: none.

reorgs.description: Kept blocks reorged because the chain took them back.

tip.description:
The node's newest block at the indexer's last read; always present,
null: no tip known yet (the job failed before its first).

chains.description: Every chain this server runs, which `POST /v1/networks` takes.

networks.description: Networks in chain, then name, order.

NetworkNode.description: One node to add, and its network.

endpoint.description: The node's URL, written as `endpoints` writes one.

routes.description: By method; each one's nodes in failover order.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

block_time_ms.description: The chain's block (slot) time, in milliseconds.

chain_id.description:
The chain's own id of the network, as its nodes report it: the EVM
chain id, the Solana or Tron genesis hash; null or empty for
Bitcoin, which the name identifies.

confirmations.description: Positions below the tip before a block counts as confirmed.

network.description:
The network's name: 1 to 64 of `a-z`, `0-9` and `-` (`my-devnet`).
Bitcoin's names its network (`mainnet`, `testnet`, `signet`,
`regtest`).

testnet.description: Whether its coins are test coins.

Recovery.description: `GET /v1/recovery`: whether a passphrase is set, never its words.

created_at.description: When it was created (Unix ms); absent when none is set.

passphrase.description:
12 BIP39 English words, space-separated. Only their hash is kept:
they are never shown again.

Report.description: The health of every indexed network.

ready.description: At least one network has an index, and no index job has a reason.

nodes.description: Nodes to append, each after its network's current ones, in order.

RpcNode.description: One stored node of a network, with its counts and state.

oneOf.description:
Its newest record while that is not an enable: what disabled it, its
`message` why. Always present, null: enabled, the transport uses it.

id.description: Its id: what a route and removal name.
Its id, newest highest; 0 until stored.

kind.description:
What: `http_401`, `http_403`, `http_404`, `rpc_{code}` (an error
object of such a code), `wrong_chain` (the node serves another
chain) or `manual` (a disable by hand), each disabling it; or
`enabled` (an enable by hand).

message.description: Why, as shown; never a URL.

RpcNodeFailureList.description:
`GET /v1/networks/{chain}/{network}/endpoints/{id}/failures`: a page of
what disabled or enabled a node.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

RpcNodeInfo.description: What a node reports about itself.

chain_id.description:
The chain it serves, as the network's `chain_id` writes it (EVM
chain id, Solana or Tron genesis hash), or its name for Bitcoin: the
network's.

RpcNodeState.description: Whether the transport uses a node.

calls.description: HTTP requests that reached it and finished.

failed_calls.description: Of those, the ones that failed.

updated_at.description: Unix ms of the last; when the node was stored if none.

url.description: The node's URL, written as `endpoints` writes one.

endpoints.description:
One to 16 distinct node URLs, in failover order. A URL carries everything:
userinfo (HTTP Basic), query keys, a key in the path,
`header.<Name>=value` parameters sent as headers, and `rpc.` settings
(`timeout_ms`, `max_request_bytes`, `max_response_bytes`, `max_batch`,
`rps`: most calls a second, e.g. `3.5`; a request waits for its turn).

RpcRoute.description: One method and the endpoints taking turns serving it.

endpoint_ids.description: The network's endpoints taking turns, by id.

method.description: The JSON-RPC method, exactly as sent, e.g. `getBlock`.

routes.description:
Every route of the network; empty: none. A method appears once, over
one or more of the network's node ids, each once.

RunJob.description: One send job of a run.

reason.description:
Why it failed, or why its last attempt is being retried; always
present.

RunOutcome.description: Where a run's jobs are together.

SecretSetting.description: A secret setting as listed: never its value or default.

description.description: What it is for: its declaration's doc comment.

Send.description:
`POST /v1/wallets/{id}/transactions` body: one payment from the path's
wallet in one asset.

amount.description: Exact positive decimal in display units.

asset.description: An asset id of the wallet's network; default `native`.

destination.description: Recipient address text, as the wallet's chain writes it.

fee.description:
How fast it should land; each chain prices it its own way. Default
`normal`.

ServerHour.description: One hour of this server's time.

failed.description: Jobs that failed for good in it.

SessionRead.description: The caller's session, decoded and checked.

amr.description:
How its login proved who it is (`pwd` or `passphrase`, then `otp`);
empty for a key's.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds; a key's bearer secret: now.

key.description: Its key, when a key issued it.

sub.description: Who it is for; always present, null: not said.

feed.description: Whether it is asked for quotes.

reason.description: Why, kept in its records (`failures`); none: `by hand`.

state.description:
`disabled`: no call goes to it, its routes skip it (a `manual`
record); `enabled`: used again, its reason cleared (an `enabled`
record).

Setting.description: A setting as listed: its key, value, default and declaration.

default.description: Its default, JSON of its type.

description.description: What it is for: its declaration's doc comment.

public.description: Whether its value may be sent in any response, to anyone.

value.description: Its value, JSON of its type; the default when never written.

settings.description:
Every setting, in declaration order: a secret one as `{key, set,
description}` only.

addresses.description: Distinct addresses indexed, keyed or watch-only.

chain.description:
The last day of chain time (up to the newest kept block), hour by
hour, oldest first.

enabled.description: Of those, how many are enabled.

server.description: The last day of this server's time, hour by hour, oldest first.

StoredNetwork.description:
One network as stored: its `network` row, its `network_asset` rows, its
routes, its index and its `network_endpoint` nodes with their counts and
state.

block_time_ms.description: The chain's block (slot) time, in milliseconds.

chain_id.description:
The chain's own id of the network (Ethereum chain id, Solana genesis
hash); always present, null where the name is enough.

confirmations.description: Positions below the tip before a block counts as confirmed.

enabled.description: Whether the server starts indexing it.

endpoints.description:
Its nodes as stored, in failover order; none enabled: no call can go
out, its index job idles and its payments wait.

explorer_address.description:
An address's explorer page, `{address}` filled in; always present,
null: none.

explorer_transaction.description:
A transaction's explorer page, `{tx}` filled in; always present,
null: none.

oneOf.description:
Its indexing; always present, null: no tip known and no index job
reason (or never indexed: not `enabled`).

max_depth.description:
How many positions below the tip a wallet's start may be; at least
`confirmations`. Always present, null: no limit. Null on a chain that
reads balances (Solana, Ethereum): its line is the chain's final block.

routes.description:
Its routed methods, each over its own nodes; every other method goes
to all of them.

settings.description: The chain's own knobs; an absent key is the chain's default.

testnet.description: Whether its coins are test coins.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

tags.description:
Tags in use on any wallet, sorted, each once. A wallet's own tags are
on it (`GET /v1/wallets`).

Transaction.description:
A kept transaction: its `transaction` row and its kept legs. The API
shows it as is. Read in one query: its legs come as a JSON array SQLite
builds (`legs`).

broadcasted_at.description:
Unix ms this server recorded it, before its first broadcast: set
exactly on this server's sends, mined or not; null on every other.
Mining keeps it.

order.description: Its position in its block; null while pending.

position.description: Its block's position; null while pending.

reason.description:
Why it reverted, when the chain said (`reverted`); null otherwise.
Stored as JSON, shown decoded.

Trigger.description: One `trigger` row; the API shows it as is.

action.description:
What it does: `{"name": "send", "input": {"source": target, "asset":
id, "destination": target, "amount": amount}}`.

check.description:
When it acts: `{"since": {"seconds": …}}` and compares under
`all`/`any`/`not`.

filter.description:
Which of them it acts on: compares under `all`/`any`/`not`; null:
every one.

group.description: The batch it was created in: every trigger of one create shares it.

oneOf.description: What its last round saw; null before its first round. Always present.

selector.description:
Which wallet indexes it acts on: `{"ids": […]}`, `{"asset": "…"}`,
`{"tag": "…"}`, `{"untagged": {}}`, `{"all": […]}`, `{"any": […]}`, `{"not": …}`.

TriggerBatch.description: `POST /v1/triggers` body: triggers of one network stored together, all or none.

triggers.description: One to 16 triggers, each with its `id`.
The batch's triggers, in its order.

TriggerDefinition.description: A trigger as written: in a `POST` (with `id`) or as a `PUT` body.

enabled.description: Absent means `true` in a `POST` and the stored value in a `PUT`.

id.description: Its slug; required in a `POST`, refused in a `PUT` (the path names it).

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

TriggerRun.description:
One run of a trigger: when it started, the send jobs it queued and how
they ended.

jobs.description: Its send jobs, in the order queued; a job no longer kept is left out.

oneOf.description: Where its jobs are together; null when none of them is kept.

stats.description:
What its round saw: wallets selected, kept by the filter, whether
the check held, and send jobs queued.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

TriggerStats.description:
What one round saw of a trigger: how many wallet indexes its selector
picked, how many of them its filter kept, whether its check held over
those, and how many effects its action returned.

checked.description: Whether its check held over the kept ones.

kept.description: How many of them its filter kept (all of them without a filter).

confirmed_at.description:
Unix ms its first code was entered; always present, null: pending,
not on yet.

code.description: The 6 digits the authenticator app shows.

uri.description: The `otpauth://` URI for an authenticator app (its QR code).

password.description:
The new password, 8 characters at least; the current one is not
asked.

disabled.description: Disabled (it, its keys and every session refused), or enabled again.

scopes.description: Its new scopes, packed, covered by the caller's.

index_state.description:
`paused`: skipped, no facts kept for blocks while paused; `indexing`:
resumed from `paused` or `no_data` (clearing its reason), backfilling
what it missed. `no_data` is the indexer's to set.

User.description:
One `user` row. Its JSON shows neither the password hash (only whether
it has one, `login`) nor the session secret.

disabled_at.description: Unix ms it was disabled: it, its keys and every session refused.

invalidated_at.description: Unix ms; every session issued in its second or before is refused.

login.description:
The argon2id hash of its password; `None`: no dashboard login. In
JSON, `login`: whether it has one.

scopes.description:
The widest scopes it may issue, packed in JSON
(`{"com.hashinbox": ["wallets.$read"]}`).

UserKey.description: One `user_key` row. Its JSON shows neither the secret nor its hash.

expires_at.description: Unix ms it stops working; `None`: never.

id.description: `hip/…`: its public client id, a session's `kid` and `iss`.

invalidated_at.description:
Unix ms; every session it issued in that second or before is
refused (rotated).

last_used_at.description: Unix ms it was last used; not kept yet.

revoked_at.description: Unix ms it was revoked: it and its sessions refused for good.

scopes.description: What it may do, covered by its user's; packed in JSON.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

key.description: The calling key, when a key calls.

oneOf.description: Its two-factor; always present, null: off.

Version.description: The server's version, and its public settings.

missing_root.description: True on a fresh install (no user yet); absent otherwise.

settings.description:
Every public setting's value (its default when never written), by
key: `{"instance": "hashinbox"}`.

version.description: The build's version: its git tag description, or the crate version.

Wallet.description:
One wallet, as the API shows it: an address, whether its key is kept,
its tags, and its indexes (each with its balances, progress and legs;
read by [`db::find`] and [`db::find_page`], empty from the other
reads). The key (`curve`, `secret`) is never serialized, and the API
reads leave it out. No `Debug`: it may hold the key.

external_id.description:
The caller's own reference for it (e.g. their customer id), 1 to 128
characters; not unique. Null when none was given.

indexes.description: Its indexes by asset id (`native` or the token id).

keyed.description: Whether this server holds its key and can send from it.

tags.description: Its tags, sorted, each once, each [`is_tag`].

WalletIndex.description:
One asset of one wallet being indexed, as every read answers it (the
API shows it as is): its columns, how far it is indexed against its
network's tip, its balances and its pending legs. All computed in SQL
(`wallet_index_with_balance`); amounts are exact atomic decimal text, never summed.
Positions are native (height or slot).

balance_confirmed.description:
Its confirmed balance: its last live mined leg's total at or below
`finality_at`, `0` without one; negative when indexed debits exceed
indexed credits (history before the start or a jump is unknown);
null while `finality_at` is unknown.

balance_confirmed_received.description:
What it had received by then (that leg's `total_received`):
`balance_confirmed` is `balance_confirmed_received -
balance_confirmed_sent` plus its adjustments.

balance_confirmed_received_usd.description:
What it had received by then in USD, each leg at its price when
mined (that leg's `total_received_usd`; a leg without one adds 0).

balance_confirmed_sent.description: What it had sent by then (fees included), the same way.

balance_confirmed_sent_usd.description: What it had sent by then in USD, the same way (`total_sent_usd`).

balance_confirmed_spendable.description:
What it can spend: `balance_confirmed` less its outgoing legs not yet
in it (pending, or mined above `finality_at`); null while
`balance_confirmed` is.

balance_pending.description:
What it will hold once every pending transaction lands: its newest
live mined leg's total, any block (`0` without one), with what this
server sent and is not mined yet, in and out; null before its first
block (`indexed_through`), as every balance is.

behind_tip.description:
Blocks between `indexed_through` and the network's produced tip;
null before the first block or without a tip.

birthday.description:
The start indexed from: the one asked for, or the first block the
node served when it no longer served that one.

finality_at.description:
The network's final (confirmed) block: its indexer's, or a trigger
round's; null when unknown.

indexed_through.description: The last block indexed; null before the first.

next_cursor.description:
Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page. Always
present.

value.description: Its new value: JSON of the setting's type.

bearer.description: A session's JWT (`POST /v1/session`), or a key's secret `his/…`. A GET route also takes the JWT as `?token=`.
